name: Should I replace pool equipment during renovation?

mainEntity.name: Is it smart to replace pumps, filters, heaters, or automation during a pool renovation?
mainEntity.text: Is it smart to replace pumps, filters, heaters, or automation during a pool renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: If equipment is already old, inefficient, noisy, or difficult to repair, renovation is usually the best time to replace it. The crew is already mobilized, plumbing and electrical work may already be part of the scope, and the finished system can be designed as a whole instead of in pieces. That often means better efficiency, fewer service calls, and cleaner equipment pad layout. For homeowners in Los Angeles, this can be especially worthwhile if the pool is being updated for energy savings, automation, or a cleaner luxury look. Still, not every piece needs replacement just because the pool is being renovated. If a component is relatively new and properly sized, it may be worth keeping. The best move is to ask for an equipment evaluation during bidding so the contractor can identify what is reusable, what is a risk, and what will likely fail soon. That way the renovation is not followed by another expensive repair six months later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replacing aging equipment during a renovation is often smart because access is already open and labor overlap can reduce future disruption. If the pump, filter, heater, or controls are near the end of their life, upgrading them during the remodel often saves time and repeated construction later.
